questions.q: Where should troubleshooting start when a secondary replica appears to have stopped synchronizing?
options: sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states.synchronization_state on the affected secondary
The SQL Server installation log only
The Windows Event Viewer Application log exclusively
The AG listener's DNS record
questions.explain: Checking the database-level synchronization_state is the first diagnostic step for a replica that has stopped synchronizing.

questions.q: What combination of DMV columns confirms a secondary is genuinely falling behind, rather than just catching up slowly?
options: log_send_queue_size and redo_queue_size both climbing over time, rather than draining
role_desc showing SECONDARY
connected_state_desc showing DISCONNECTED only
last_hardened_time showing a recent timestamp
questions.explain: If both queue sizes are climbing rather than shrinking, that confirms data is genuinely backing up, not just working through a temporary backlog.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the listener "not resolving" almost always caused by?
options: DNS propagation issues, cluster name object (CNO) permission problems, or a firewall blocking the listener port — rarely the AG configuration itself
The AG's databases being in the wrong recovery model
The primary replica running out of disk space
SQL Server Standard Edition licensing restrictions
questions.explain: Listener resolution problems are typically infrastructure issues (DNS, AD permissions for the CNO, firewall rules) rather than problems with the AG itself.

questions.q: Why does the WSFC deliberately refuse to trigger automatic failover when it has lost quorum, even with a healthy synchronous secondary available?
options: To prevent a split-brain scenario where multiple nodes could believe they are primary at the same time
Because quorum loss automatically deletes the Availability Group
Because synchronous replicas are incompatible with quorum-based clusters
There is no such behavior — quorum loss has no effect on failover
questions.explain: Refusing to act without quorum is a deliberate safety mechanism to avoid split-brain, where two nodes might independently believe they're the primary.

questions.q: An expected automatic failover didn't happen despite a healthy synchronous, automatic-failover-mode secondary being available. What should be checked first, per this lesson?
options: WSFC quorum state — the cluster may have deliberately withheld failover due to quorum loss, not because the AG configuration is wrong
Whether the database is in BULK_LOGGED recovery model
Whether backup compression is enabled
Whether the listener has an SSL certificate configured
questions.explain: Quorum status should be checked before assuming the AG itself is misconfigured, since a cluster without quorum will not fail over automatically even under otherwise-ideal conditions.
